## Why visit

The timber-framed building is a striking contrast to the tiled Victorian pubs elsewhere in Manchester. It deserves a visit for that architectural story, including its relocation during redevelopment, with a cask selection that gives beer drinkers a reason to go inside. The present pub is operated by Nicholson’s and has substantial dining space, so expect a busier visitor-oriented setting than a backstreet local. Pair it with neighbouring Sinclair’s and the Shudehill pubs to compare very different approaches to traditional beer and historic buildings.

## Plan the visit

Historic building does not mean an untouched historic pub interior. Outdoor service may require plastic glasses; choose indoors if the room is the purpose.

**Getting there:** Near Manchester Victoria and Exchange Square; adjacent to Sinclair’s Oyster Bar.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
